results.title: Taiwanese hit character CAPOO takes over Seoul tourism campaign
results.content: A six-legged cartoon cat-insect hybrid from Taiwan is taking on Seoul's biggest tourist attractions, as the city turns to an overseas character franchise to reach new audiences and draw more visitors from one of its key travel markets. The Seoul Tourism Organization said Tuesday it has partnered with CAPOO, a popular Taiwanese character, for Visit Seoul's first collaboration with an overseas character intellectual property brand. Running from Nov. 23–27, the campaign features three short videos following CAPOO on visits to some of Seoul's best-known attractions, combining Korean traditions, food and unusual travel experiences. In the first video, scheduled for Nov. 19, CAPOO wears traditional Korean hanbok while exploring Gyeongbok Palace and its architecture. results.title: Mom's Touch opens 2nd Japanese franchise, targets 11 stores by year-end
results.content: Mom’s Touch is stepping up its expansion in Japan, opening its second locally franchised restaurant this week as the Korean burger and chicken chain aims to build a network of 11 outlets by the end of the year. The company said Wednesday that Mom’s Touch Itabashi Station will open Friday in Tokyo’s Kita ward, marking its seventh store in Japan and first franchise opening since relocating its Japanese corporate office to Shinjuku in September. Located near the east exit of Itabashi Station on the JR Saikyo Line, the restaurant targets neighborhood residents, office workers and commuters traveling into central Tokyo. Unlike existing company-operated outlets in commercial districts such as Shibuya and Harajuku, the new restaurant is designed to serve everyday dining needs, including casual meals and family outings, through its combination of burgers, chicken and pizza. results.title: Kolmar Korea turns to AI to predict skin safety before cosmetics hit market
results.content: Kolmar Korea is developing artificial intelligence (AI) technology to predict how cosmetic ingredients affect the skin before products are manufactured, in a move aimed at speeding development and strengthening the global competitiveness of its clients. The cosmetics manufacturer said Wednesday that it signed a memorandum of understanding with the Korea Research Institute of Chemical Technology on Tuesday to jointly develop AI-based technology for predicting skin effects. The agreement was signed by Moon Byung-seok, head of technology research at Kolmar Holdings, and Shin Seok-min, president of the Korea Research Institute of Chemical Technology. The two organizations will collaborate on research, technical exchanges and performance assessments to develop AI models capable of predicting skin reactions and ingredient absorption. results.title: K-culture gets festive makeover at Korea tourism souvenir fair
results.content: Korea is turning its souvenirs into a festive attraction, bringing 143 companies and institutions together for a three-day fair designed to connect the country's cultural products with visitors and global buyers. The Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism and the Korea Tourism Organization (KTO) will host the 2026 Korea Tourism Souvenir Fair from Nov. 20–22 at Dongdaemun Design Plaza in Seoul. Now in its fifth year, the event will be its largest yet, with participation up about 60 percent from last year and 145 exhibition booths showcasing products across design, crafts, fashion, beauty, food and lifestyle categories. This year's theme, “A K-Goods Village Covered in First Snow,” combines traditional Korean colors and patterns with Christmas decorations, with a character called Santa Daegam guiding visitors through the exhibition. results.title: Musinsa Standard brings minimalist fashion to Jeju Island
results.content: Musinsa Standard is bringing its minimalist fashion aesthetic to Jeju Island, opening its first store there as the Korean clothing brand looks to attract both local shoppers and international tourists. The store, located in Donam-dong, Jeju City, will open Nov. 26, marking the brand's 45th domestic location and expanding its retail presence beyond mainland Korea. To mark the opening, Musinsa Standard is introducing 12 limited-edition T-shirt designs developed with local brands Jeju Samdasoo, Bbang Gomi and Slowcoaster. The collection draws on familiar symbols of Jeju, including tangerines, hallabong citrus fruit and dol hareubang stone statues. results.title: SK Chemicals, Seogwipo join hands to recycle waste banners
results.content: SK Chemicals is partnering with Seogwipo City on Jeju Island to establish a circular system that turns discarded banners into new products for reuse in the local community. The company said Wednesday that it has signed a memorandum of understanding with the city to promote the recycling and reuse of waste banners. The ceremony was attended by Seogwipo Mayor Kim Hee-chan and Ko Jeong-seok, head of SK Chemicals' recycling business division, among other officials. The partnership stems from an idea developed during a community problem-solving competition hosted by the Ministry of the Interior and Safety and the Korea Chamber of Commerce and Industry in September. Seogwipo joined a consortium that took on a waste banner recycling challenge proposed by SK Chemicals. results.content: Korea ended the year with a 1-0 win over Qatar on Tuesday as Oh Se-hun headed the only goal of the game. It was a dominant performance and really should have been a more convincing win but the strikers missed chance after chance and the opposing goalkeeper made save after save. Indeed, Qatar was so bad that it took a little sheen off the win. Regardless, it was welcome after losing 3-2 to Saudi Arabia last Friday. This was not just the last game of 2026, but it was the last game of Robert Moreno’s coaching contract. results.title: Trump 'serious' about engaging with N. Korean leader Kim: Rubio
results.content: U.S. President Donald Trump is "serious" about engaging with North Korean leader Kim Jong-un, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Wednesday. "If we have a problem with North Korea, the only way we are going to solve it is by meeting with them," Rubio told the traveling White House press pool.

results.title: Elsevier chairman urges universities to pair optimism with focus, trust
results.content: Youngsuk “YS” Chi, chairman of Dutch academic publisher Elsevier, urged university leaders Wednesday to meet mounting pressures — from tight budgets to artificial intelligence (AI) — with what he called optimism backed by thoughtful action. Chi gave the keynote on the second day of the Innovation & Impact Summit 2026, which Times Higher Education (THE) is holding at Korea University in Seoul from Tuesday to Thursday. The London-based publication is known for its annual World University Rankings. “Many of you are facing tighter budgets. Geopolitical tension is making it harder to work across borders. AI is changing how research is done faster than anyone can write the rules about it,” Chi said. “None of these pressures is new on its own. results.content: Samsung Electro-Mechanics has revised its existing supply agreement with Nvidia to expand supplies of advanced semiconductor package substrates and multilayer ceramic capacitors (MLCCs) for the U.S. chipmaker's artificial intelligence (AI) computing platforms, the Korean company said Wednesday. The two sides announced their strategic partnership last month, under which Samsung Electro-Mechanics agreed to supply advanced package substrates for Nvidia's computing and high-speed networking products. results.title: Korea launches advanced 3,600-ton frigate equipped with homegrown radar
results.content: Korea launched a new 3,600-ton guided-missile frigate equipped with domestically developed stealth sensors and radar systems on Wednesday, bolstering its coastal defense capabilities in the West Sea as the country accelerates its push to become a major global arms exporter. The ROKS Pyeongtaek, the fifth ship in the Navy’s Ulsan-class Batch-III program, entered the water during a ceremony at Hanwha Ocean’s shipyard on the southern island of Geoje, according to the Navy and the Defense Acquisition Program Administration. Designed and built entirely in Korea, the 129-meter warship is slated to replace the Navy’s aging fleet of older frigates and corvettes. Following sea trials, it will be delivered to the Navy in December 2027 for operational deployment. results.title: Korea considering unannounced disaster alerts during CSAT to catch AI-assisted cheaters
results.content: The government is considering sending unannounced disaster alert messages during this week's annual college entrance exam to catch cheaters using their phones and prevent artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted cheating, an interior ministry official said Wednesday. Authorities have been mulling measures to root out cheating during the College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT) on Thursday following a recent cheating scandal in the certified tax accountant exam using AI. As part of anti-cheating measures unveiled Tuesday, the government said it would send an emergency alert message, designed to reach most mobile phones and sound a loud alarm even when muted, before the start of the exam to detect any unsubmitted devices. results.title: Lee to hold talks with Xi on sidelines of APEC summit
results.content: Korean President Lee Jae Myung was set to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping on Wednesday to discuss ways to enhance bilateral cooperation. The meeting comes as Lee arrived in Shenzhen, China, earlier in the day to attend the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, which runs through Thursday. The upcoming talks mark the two leaders' third bilateral summit, following their first meeting in November in Gyeongju, the Korean city that hosted the 2025 APEC summit. They last met in Beijing in January when Lee visited China. During Wednesday's meeting, Lee and Xi are expected to assess progress in bilateral relations and discuss ways to expand trade and investment, as well as people-to-people and cultural exchanges, Lee's spokesperson Kim Sung-wan said in a press release. results.title: HYBE partners with Creative Artists Agency to expand global reach
results.content: HYBE, the Korean entertainment powerhouse behind K-pop sensation BTS, is joining forces with one of Hollywood's most influential talent agencies in a strategic partnership aimed at expanding its artists' global reach and opening new business opportunities across entertainment, sports and brand development. The partnership, announced Monday, brings together HYBE's artist roster and intellectual property with Creative Artists Agency's (CAA) international network and industry expertise. The companies agreed to develop business opportunities using HYBE's artists and content assets while jointly pursuing broader corporate initiatives. results.content: Korean stocks traded slightly lower late Wednesday morning, as retail investors sold shares following an early rally fueled by upbeat earnings from U.S. chip giant Nvidia. After opening 2.62 percent higher, the benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI) reversed its early gains, falling 6.9 points, or 0.14 percent, to 4,961.58 as of 11:20 a.m. The index fell below the psychologically important 5,000-point level Tuesday for the first time in about nine months as foreign investors continued to sell technology shares. Overnight, Wall Street closed lower, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average falling 1.64 percent and the S&P 500 losing 1.03 percent. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite declined 0.74 percent. results.title: Korea issues cybersecurity advisory after flaws discovered in Java platform
results.content: Korea's science ministry advised companies Wednesday to carry out emergency security checks and update their systems after vulnerabilities were discovered in the widely used Java programming language. The vulnerabilities found in OpenJDK, an open-source implementation of the Java Platform, could allow malicious actors to execute malware on affected systems, the Ministry of Science and ICT said. Oracle Corp., the company that maintains Java, said it is preparing to release security patches for 11 vulnerabilities, which it evaluates at a CVSS 3.1 severity score of 8.1, the second-highest in its four-tier system. Java is widely used to develop Android applications, banking systems, cloud services and other software. results.title: Russia to unveil monument honoring N. Korean troops' contribution in Kursk this year: KCNA
results.content: Russian President Vladimir Putin has said Moscow plans to unveil a monument this year honoring North Korean troops participating in Russia's war with Ukraine, according to Pyongyang's state media Wednesday. Putin made the remarks Monday while meeting Jo Yong-won, a secretary of the Central Committee of the ruling Workers' Party of Korea and a close aide to leader Kim Jong-un, the Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) said, citing Russia's Tass news agency. "Russia is planning to unveil a monument to the common feats of the Russian army and the KPA in Kursk within this year," the KCNA quoted Putin as saying. KPA stands for the Korean People's Army, the North's armed forces. results.title: Fishing boat carrying 7 goes missing off west coast
results.content: A fishing boat carrying seven people went missing off the west coast Wednesday, with search efforts under way, the Coast Guard said. The 7.93-ton vessel was reported out of reach shortly after 1 a.m., two days after it left a port in Taean, about 110 kilometers southwest of Seoul. The Coast Guard said it has activated a rescue headquarters and sent nine patrol boats and two aircraft to the scene while requesting help from nearby civilian vessels and the Navy. Interior Minister Yun Ho-jung asked the oceans ministry, the Coast Guard and the relevant local governments to use all available equipment and personnel to quickly and safely rescue those on board, according to his office.

results.title: KBS epic 'Sword & Silence' revisits how small states survive among great powers
results.content: As leaders of the United States, China and Russia prepare to sit down together for a trilateral summit this week, a historical drama about a small kingdom caught between great powers has arrived on Korean television. KBS TV’s new period drama “Sword & Silence,” known in Korean as “Munmu,” premiered Saturday. It follows King Munmu (626-681 A.D.) as he unites the kingdoms of Silla, Goguryeo and Baekje on the Korean Peninsula before confronting his former ally, the Tang dynasty (618-907) of ancient China, one of the world’s then-superpowers. The 28-episode series reportedly cost around 30 billion won ($21 million), the largest budget ever for a KBS epic. The series is also streaming globally on Netflix. The timing is hard to ignore. results.content: As concerns mount over the potential misuse of artificial intelligence (AI) glasses in Korea, where fears of AI-assisted cheating have gripped the nation ahead of the College Scholastic Ability Test, device makers, including Samsung Electronics, are facing a growing dilemma. results.title: Korea emerges as new outlet for China's excess EV capacity
results.content: China’s mounting electric vehicle (EV) overcapacity is driving its automakers to Korea in search of new growth, as fierce domestic competition and tougher trade barriers in Europe narrow their options for expansion. Chinese automakers are no longer treating Korea simply as a market for exporting finished vehicles. BYD, Zeekr and XPeng are strengthening their local operations and hiring Korean executives with experience at established foreign automakers — in a push to turn Korea into a more permanent overseas market. The shift comes as China’s EV industry faces fierce price competition and a crowded domestic market, leaving automakers under growing pressure to find additional demand abroad. Europe, once a key destination for Chinese EVs, has also become more difficult to penetrate due to higher tariffs and tighter regulatory scrutiny. results.title: Seoul looks to night to unlock new economic growth
results.content: Time can constrain a city just as space does. With daytime hours already crowded with work, commerce and competing demands on urban space, Seoul is now looking to a less-explored source of economic growth: the hours after dark. The city’s nighttime economy initiative seeks to put existing sports facilities, cultural venues and parks to fuller use, connecting them with transport and neighborhood businesses. The ambition is not simply to keep shops open longer, but to rethink how the city can serve its people differently at different hours, according to Lee Ji-hyun, a special adviser to Seoul Mayor Oh Se-hoon for nighttime economy. “The space is the same, whether it is day or night,” Lee, who took the post in September, said in an interview with The Korea Times. “But we haven’t looked at it through the lens of time.” Cheonggye Stream, for example, offers a different experience at night tha

results.title: [K-LIT REVIEW] Life lessons from Min Jin Lee's 'American Hagwon'
results.content: Is "American Hagwon" an engrossing story wrapped in a cultural lesson, or is it the other way around? And does it matter, when the story is this good and when one can learn so much from it? Readers who enjoyed Korean American author Min Jin Lee’s "Pachinko" will be pleased to find some of the same narrative structure applied to her latest story. Yes, it could be called a soap opera, but when a soap opera is great, it holds attention. Focusing on the Koh family, the story spans a generation and three countries. The family oscillates between Korea, the United States and Australia, often living apart as they pursue educational opportunities, job postings and economic security. The parents, Helen and John, are living a familiar life pattern of working as hard as they can to do all they can for their children, Bo, DH and Mido. results.title: Lee arrives in Shenzhen for APEC summit
results.content: SHENZHEN, China — South Korean President Lee Jae Myung arrived in Shenzhen, China, on Wednesday to attend this week's Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit. During his stay through Thursday, Lee is scheduled to participate in the APEC CEO summit, a welcoming dinner hosted by Chinese President Xi Jinping and the main summit session, which will be held under the theme, "Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together." The APEC summit is expected to coincide with a high-profile meeting among U.S. President Donald Trump, Xi and Russian President Vladimir Putin, who are likely to discuss nuclear arms reduction among other international issues. results.content: DOHA — The tumultuous year of 2026 came to an end for the men's national football team with a narrow victory over Qatar on Tuesday in Doha, where the Taegeuk Warriors failed to capitalize on numerous chances. Forward Oh Se-hun's 43rd-minute header was the lone goal in South Korea's 1-0 victory at Abdullah bin Khalifa Stadium in the Qatari capital. South Korea peppered Qatar with 22 shot attempts and nine shots on goal, as their attackers took advantage of open space afforded by Qatar's passive defense. Compared to some earlier matches, the South Koreans exhibited more efficient off-the-ball movements and made plays in the attacking third with purpose. However, the two starting forwards, Oh and Son Heung-min, lacked the clinical finishing touch. results.content: DOHA — South Korea blanked Qatar 1-0 in Doha on Tuesday in their final men's football friendly of the year, prevailing in a match much more lopsided than the final score indicated. Striker Oh Se-hun headed home the match's lone goal late in the first half at Abdullah bin Khalifa Stadium in the Qatari capital, where South Korea, ranked 32nd, held 60th-ranked Qatar without a shot in the first half and finished with a 22-2 advantage in shot attempts. results.title: Lee heads to China for APEC after wrapping up ASEAN summit
results.content: MANILA — South Korean President Lee Jae Myung departed for China on Tuesday to attend the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, wrapping up his trip to Manila for the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) summit. Lee, who arrived in Manila on Monday, attended the South Korea-ASEAN summit, a gathering with the five Mekong countries — Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand and Vietnam — as well as the ASEAN Plus Three summit involving ASEAN, South Korea, China and Japan. During the meetings, the president stressed the need for closer regional cooperation in responding to complex crises and called for the region's support for his administration's policy of seeking peaceful coexistence on the Korean Peninsula. results.title: 3.6 magnitude earthquake hits city in southeastern S. Korea: weather agency
results.content: A 3.6 magnitude earthquake struck a city in the southeastern province of North Gyeongsang on Tuesday, the weather agency said. The quake hit an area about 22 kilometers northwest of Sangju's city center around 11:10 p.m. with the epicenter located at a depth of 20 km, according to the Korea Meteorological Administration (KMA). The agency initially put the magnitude at 3.7 but revised it down to 3.6 after further analysis. It was the strongest of the 58 earthquakes recorded on the Korean Peninsula and in surrounding waters this year. It was also the first quake of magnitude 3.5 or higher in the region in about 18 months, since a magnitude 3.7 tremor struck waters 52 km northwest of Taean in South Chungcheong Province on May 5 last year.
